_comment: Static source of truth for the Reservoir Storage outcome domain. Note: the metric ID 'resevoir_storage' preserves the existing spelling in the dashboard UI (scripts.js) and must not be corrected here, as the filename must match the UI's fetch path.

outcome.name: Reservoir Storage
outcome.definition: The volume of water held in California's major surface water reservoirs, measured relative to historical averages, capacity, and operational targets defined by water rights permits, project operations criteria, and environmental requirements. This outcome domain captures how California water law and regulatory frameworks shape reservoir operations—through water right permit conditions, environmental flow requirements, hydropower licensing obligations, and drought management rules. Legal standards rarely specify target storage volumes directly; instead, they impose inflow, outflow, and operational requirements that collectively determine how much water is stored at any point in time.
outcome.tier_interpretation_note: These tiers reflect reservoir storage conditions across California's major water storage facilities relative to historical averages and capacity. Legal standards affect this outcome by shaping inflow requirements, mandatory releases, and operational constraints at major reservoirs. Each tier entry identifies a legal standard whose mechanism is classified as either direct (a clear operational or regulatory pathway that affects reservoir storage) or indirect (a conditional, secondary, or system-level influence on storage levels).

tiers.threshold: Reservoir storage is greater than or equal to the top threshold for each reservoir for at least 90% of years (as represented by April values) in the dataset; As of July 2025, this threshold is set at the 50th percentile of recent historical data as available through CDEC

Tier 2 Reservoir storage is greater than or equal to the middle threshold for each reservoir for at least 67% of years (as represented by April values) in the dataset; As of July 2025, this threshold is set at the 33rd percentile of recent historical data as available through CDEC

Tier 3 Reservoir storage is greater than or equal to the middle threshold for each reservoir for at least 30% of years (as represented by April values) in the dataset; As of July 2025, this threshold is set at the 33rd percentile of recent historical data as available through CDEC

Tier 4 Reservoir storage is not high enough to meet the conditions of Tiers 1-3. Reservoir storage is below the middle threshold (at or below the lower threshold) for more than 70% of years (as represented by April values). As of July 2025, the lower threshold is set as the 20th percentile of recent historical values

legal_standards._comment: Canonical legal standard IDs for this outcome domain.

standards.title: SWRCB Water Right Permits — Reservoir Storage and Release Conditions
standards.citation: State Water Resources Control Board water right permits for major reservoirs
standards.scope_note: Water right permits for major reservoirs specify storage capacities, diversion seasons, and conditions of use; permit conditions may include mandatory bypass flows, minimum pool requirements, and release schedules that directly affect how much water can be stored.

standards.title: Endangered Species Act — Reservoir and Dam Operation Constraints
standards.citation: Endangered Species Act §7; Biological Opinions for major federal dams (NMFS, USFWS)
standards.scope_note: Biological Opinions for federally operated or licensed dams impose flow release requirements, temperature management protocols, and reservoir level restrictions to protect listed anadromous fish and other species; these requirements can significantly constrain storage flexibility.

standards.title: FERC Hydropower License — Reservoir Operation and Flow Conditions
standards.citation: Federal Power Act §10(j); FERC license conditions for California hydropower facilities
standards.scope_note: FERC licenses governing hydropower operations at major dams include mandatory minimum flow releases, ramping rate requirements, and reservoir level conditions that affect how storage is managed throughout the year and during drought periods.

standards.title: Central Valley Project Improvement Act — Reservoir Management Requirements
standards.scope_note: CVPIA requirements for fish and wildlife restoration impose constraints on CVP reservoir operations including Shasta, Folsom, and Trinity, affecting storage through mandatory cold water pool maintenance, minimum downstream flow releases, and water dedication to environmental purposes.

standards.title: Drought Emergency Regulations — Reservoir Conservation and Curtailment
standards.citation: California Water Code; Governor's drought emergency declarations; SWRCB emergency regulations
standards.scope_note: During declared drought emergencies, state regulations may impose mandatory conservation targets, restrict diversions to reservoirs, or modify operational requirements; these actions can affect both the rate of storage decline and the management of remaining stored water.

standards.title: California Wild and Scenic Rivers Act
standards.citation: California Public Resources Code §5093.50 et seq.
standards.scope_note: Designates certain river segments as wild and scenic, prohibiting construction of dams and diversions that would substantially alter the river's free-flowing character; limits future reservoir development on designated rivers and constrains operational changes that would affect protected reaches.
